Charge Balance Calculation

Source: R/geochemistry.R
charge_balance.Rd

Calculates the ionic charge balance of major-ion chemistry data.

charge_balance(df, ...)

# S3 method for class 'data.frame'
charge_balance(df, location, analyte, result, unit, date, ...)

# S3 method for class 'env_schema'
charge_balance(df, analyte_matching = c("exact", "strict", "normalized"))

Arguments

df

A data frame or `env_schema` object.

...

Additional arguments passed to methods.

location

Location identifier column.

analyte

Analyte column.

result

Analytical result column.

unit

Reporting unit column.

date

Sample date column.

analyte_matching

Analyte matching strategy. One of `"exact"`, `"strict"`, or `"normalized"`.

Value

A data frame containing:

  • location identifiers;

  • sample dates;

  • total cations (meq/L);

  • total anions (meq/L);

  • charge balance percentage.

Details

`charge_balance()` is an S3 generic that supports both raw data frames and `env_schema` objects.

For data frames, environmental column mappings must be supplied. For `env_schema` objects, mapped schema fields are used automatically.

Charge balance is calculated using concentrations converted to milliequivalents per liter (meq/L) and provides a quality-control evaluation of analytical completeness and consistency.

For data frames, `charge_balance()` first converts the supplied data to an `env_schema` object using the specified column mappings and then dispatches to [charge_balance.env_schema()].

Charge balance is calculated from the sum of major dissolved cations and anions after conversion to milliequivalents per liter (meq/L).

Major ions used in the calculation include:

  • calcium;

  • magnesium;

  • sodium;

  • potassium;

  • chloride;

  • sulfate;

  • bicarbonate (alkalinity).

The charge balance percentage is calculated as:

$$ 100 \times \frac{\sum cations - \sum anions} {\sum cations + \sum anions} $$

Values near zero generally indicate internally consistent analytical results, whereas large positive or negative values may indicate analytical error, missing constituents, transcription errors, or unit-conversion problems.

For `env_schema` objects, analyte, result, unit, date, and location fields are obtained directly from schema mappings.

Analyte Matching

exact

Uses analyte names exactly as reported.

strict

Applies text normalization while preserving analytical distinctions such as dissolved versus total fractions.

normalized

Resolves analyte aliases to canonical analyte names using package analyte metadata.

Output Structure

One record is returned for each unique location and sample-date combination.

When multiple measurements of the same analyte occur within a location and sample-date group, values are averaged during geochemical standardization prior to charge-balance calculation.

Returned cation and anion totals are expressed in milliequivalents per liter (meq/L).

Interpretation

Typical charge balance error guidelines are:

< ±5%

Excellent agreement.

±5% to ±10%

Generally acceptable for most environmental investigations.

> ±10%

May indicate incomplete chemistry or analytical issues and should be reviewed.

These thresholds should be interpreted in the context of project objectives, laboratory methods, and sample chemistry.

Validation

Input data are validated for:

  • analyte resolution;

  • major-ion chemistry availability;

  • supported analytical units;

  • successful conversion to milliequivalents;

  • duplicate analyte measurements.

Examples

charge_balance(gw)
